speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You presented with right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision; can you describe exactly how your leg is positioned and how the pain feels?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning. Can you tell me if your right leg was forced into a specific position, such as the knee being bent while the foot points downward, or if you felt a "popping" sensation when the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of your right leg being shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated is a classic presentation for a femoral neck fracture. Did you hear or feel a specific "pop" or snap at the moment of the accident before the pain became severe? REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvis_X-Ray

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Hemoconcentration and CBC. REQUEST TEST: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Femoral Neck Fracture. The clinical presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg following high-energy trauma, combined with immediate severe groin pain, is pathognomonic for this injury.
